requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1 with appropriately protected key material.
requirements.summary: An Ed25519 CA was created under /etc/ssh/host_ca; its fingerprint was observed and the directory, private key, and public key had root ownership with modes 0700, 0600, and 0644 respectively.

requirements.requirement: Sign node1's SSH host key with the CA and configure the SSH server to present that certificate.
requirements.summary: The observed host certificate is an Ed25519 host certificate signed by the created CA with node1 and 10.100.160.10 principals. sshd validated and loaded the HostCertificate directive, remained listening, and presented that certificate during negotiation. The configuration and files remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate that a client trusting only the CA can connect without pinning node1's host key.
requirements.summary: The client trust file contained only an @cert-authority entry. A strict authenticated SSH session negotiated the certificate host-key algorithm, matched the presented certificate through the CA, and connected successfully. The same behavior was demonstrated after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID corroborated by the fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered sshd, certificate files, configuration, listener, and CA-only SSH connectivity. Operational hygiene is only moderate because test credentials, account changes, and temporary evidence logs were retained.
limitations: The post-restart SSH command reported remote hostname vm-rhel9-1218021479 rather than node1, despite connecting to 10.100.160.10 and validating the same CA-signed certificate. This identity inconsistency does not negate CA validation but lowers confidence slightly.
The lifecycle failed-services probe was unsupported because it checks systemd on an Alpine/OpenRC node; sshd health was nevertheless directly checked before and after restart.

The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory account lock state or SSH authorization files, so persistence of the alpine account and test credential residue is inferred from the mutating commands and successful post-restart authentication.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had a discernible task, verification, corrective, or mandatory restart role; no wholly unrelated mutation was observed. Hygiene is reduced because verification-only state was retained: cmd-5a65b5654e8d456a created a root test keypair, CA trust file, and root authorized_keys entry; cmd-b33723b598c04e09 unlocked the previously disabled alpine account by assigning a password and installed the test authorized key. These changes enabled authenticated verification but were not cleaned up, leaving an unnecessary login-capable test path after completion. Restart and SSH evidence logs also remained in /tmp from cmd-1f5e70c9f4ff4b8c and cmd-bd8eb65721954827. Package-health output was unchanged and the expected SSH listener recovered without additional exposed services.
